Matcha On Ice Cafe — Equipment & Bar Manual

I

The Grinder

Fiorenzato F64 Evo Pro

The F64 Evo Pro is a commercial on-demand grinder — it grinds fresh for each dose rather than sitting pre-ground in a hopper, dosed through a touchscreen rather than a mechanical doser. Grind size is set with a stepless, micrometric adjustment ring, so there are no click-stops to count: adjust in small turns and grind a test amount before committing a full dose.

This unit has the PRO quick-release chamber, which pulls apart without tools for a deeper daily clean — see the Daily Cleaning steps below.

Specifications

Burr Size64 mm
Burr TypeFlat
DosingOn-demand
AdjustmentStepless (no click-stops)
ChamberPRO quick-release

Daily Startup

  1. Make sure the power switch (rear/side, marked O/I) is in O (off) before plugging in.
  2. Plug into a grounded outlet and flip the switch to I (on). The display boots to the Home screen after a few seconds.
  3. Load beans. close the locking slide under the hopper, seat the hopper on top and tighten the fastening screw, remove the hopper lid and fill with beans, replace the lid, then gradually open the locking slide so beans feed into the grinding chamber.
  4. The grinder is now ready to dose.

Dosing Modes (Settings → Technical Settings → Operating Mode)

ModeHow It Works
Standard (default)Press the dose button to select it, then trigger by pressing the portafilter into the activation microswitch under the fork.
DirectPress the dose button and grinding starts immediately — no portafilter switch needed.
AutomaticNo dose buttons — press the portafilter switch once for single, twice quickly for double, three times for triple.
PreselectionSelect the dose (stays selected), then press the portafilter switch once to start; stays selected for repeat use.

Manual grinding (hold the button) works independently of the mode above, for continuous or free-pour grinding. Dose times are adjustable under Settings → Change dose times — single dose 1.0–12.0 sec, double dose 1.0–25.0 sec (±0.1 sec tolerance), saved automatically on exit.

Adjusting Grind Size

  1. Press and hold the adjustment lock lever, on the back of the disk just under the hopper.
  2. Turn the disk — clockwise for coarser, counter-clockwise for finer.
  3. Release the lever to re-lock the disk in position.

You can adjust while the motor is running. Grind is stepless and micrometric, so small turns matter — grind a small test amount after each adjustment to check before committing to a full dose.

Daily Cleaning — End of Shift

  1. Power off and unplug before cleaning.
  2. Close the locking slide, loosen the hopper fastening screw, and remove the hopper.
  3. Remove the hopper lid, empty remaining beans back into their original bag, and seal it.
  4. Wash the hopper (inside and outside) with warm water and a pH-neutral, unscented, food-safe degreaser — no abrasive sponges or aggressive detergents, not dishwasher-safe. Dry thoroughly with a soft cloth.
  5. Grinding chamber. use a soft, clean/sanitized brush and vacuum only to remove coffee residue. Never use water or detergent inside the chamber or on the burrs.
  6. Loosen the screw and pull out the coffee discharge tube (chute). Wash it with warm water and the same food-safe degreaser, dry with a soft cloth, and vacuum out the tube housing.
  7. Wipe the exterior body with a soft cloth and food-safe cleaner only — no abrasive sponges, no water or steam jets on the machine body.
  8. Reassemble: discharge tube back in and screwed down, then hopper back on and screwed down, then lid on. Refill with beans for the next shift.
  9. Check the power cable, visually and by touch, for cuts, exposed wire, or plug damage. Replace only with an identical cable type if damaged.

Daily Cleaning — PRO Quick-Release Chamber

  1. Close the slide, unscrew and remove the bean hopper.
  2. Vacuum loose beans and powder from the chamber collar.
  3. Release the two quick-lock levers and pull out the removable chamber.
  4. Brush-clean (soft, sanitized brush) the removable chamber and the fixed upper burr attached to it — dry only, no water or detergent, not dishwasher-safe.
  5. Remove the anti-clumping foil blade, wash it with warm water and food-safe degreaser, and dry it.
  6. Vacuum and brush-clean the main grinding chamber and the lower (mobile) burr — dry only.
  7. Reinstall in order: foil blade, then the removable chamber (lock both levers fully closed), then the hopper.
  • The grinder will not start unless both quick-release levers are fully closed — two internal microswitches block the motor otherwise.
  • Wear gloves when handling the burrs — edges are sharp.

Monthly Deep Clean

  1. Do this after the end-of-shift clean — the chamber must be completely empty of coffee, hopper detached.
  2. Pour a dose of a commercial grinder-cleaning product (e.g. Puly Grind or similar food-safe grinder cleaner, in grain/crystal form) into the empty grinding chamber.
  3. Run a grinding cycle — the product scrubs coffee oils, scale and rancid residue off the burrs without disassembly or losing the grind setting.

Burr Replacement

A warning icon appears near the logo on the Home screen when the burrs are approaching their scheduled replacement point (based on hours of use or kg ground). You can keep grinding until the limit is reached; remaining life can be checked anytime under Settings → "Replacing the grinders."

Burr replacement itself must be done by a qualified operator or technician using original Fiorenzato parts. After replacement, run "Reset Grinder" from Settings to zero the usage counter.

Quick Troubleshooting

ProblemLikely CauseFix
Won't power onNo powerCheck the switch is on "I", check the circuit breaker, check cable/outlet.
Beans won't drop into chamberLocking slide closedOpen the slide.
Grinder won't start (PRO models)Quick-release levers not fully closedClose both levers completely.
Settings lost on restartBackup battery flatContact service to replace the battery.
Motor stops mid-grindThermal cutout tripped — foreign object jammed the burrsPower off, unplug, let cool, open the chamber, remove the hopper, clear the obstruction, reassemble, retry.
Warning icon on displayBurrs near end of rated lifePlan replacement — the grinder still works until the limit hits.

If any issue persists after these steps, contact the dealer rather than opening the machine further — anything involving the motor or electronics is technician-only.

Daily Checklist

Opening

  • Power on
  • Fill hopper if needed
  • Dial in grind on the first shots of the day — taste/pull test shots

Closing

  • Power off, unplug
  • Empty and wash hopper
  • Brush/vacuum grinding chamber — no water
  • Remove, wash, dry and reinsert discharge tube
  • Wipe down exterior
  • Check power cable condition
  • Reassemble and refill for next shift
II

The Espresso Machine

Sanremo Zoe Compact 208V, 2 Group

The Zoe Compact is a heat-exchanger, volumetric-control 2-group machine — it brews and steams simultaneously from a single boiler. This section assumes the SED (electronic/programmable) control panel.

Voltage. this unit is wired for 208V (standard US 3-phase-derived commercial voltage) rather than the EU 220–240V spec in the base manual — operation and controls are identical, only the electrical hookup differs. Confirm amp draw and breaker sizing against the unit's own rating label, not EU figures.

Specifications

Groups2
System TypeHeat exchanger (brew + steam simultaneously)
Boiler Capacity7 litres (copper)
Boiler Working Pressure0.8–1 bar
Coffee Delivery Pressure8–9 bar
Max Mains Water Pressure6 bar (install a pressure reducer if higher)
Dimensions (W × D × H)530 × 528 × 543 mm
Net Weight~45 kg

Controls Reference

ControlFunction
B — Steam knobsTwo on this 2-group; turn counter-clockwise to open, clockwise to close.
C — Hot water spoutDispenses hot water, controlled by M6.
D — Main power switch0 = Off · 1 = Pump + electronics on · 2 = + heating element on.
E — PortafilterHolds the filter basket; twist counter-clockwise into the group to lock.
F — Group headThe portafilter seat where shots brew.
M1–M4 — Dose buttons (SED)Short single, long single, short double, long double.
M5 — Continuous / manualStarts and stops a manual pour; also the programming button.
M6 — Hot water buttonPress to start, press again to stop.
N — Pump pressure gaugeShows pump/extraction pressure while pulling a shot.
P — Boiler pressure gaugeDouble gauge — shows both boiler and pump pressure.
T — Cup warmer switchIf fitted, powers the cup-warming surface.

Daily Startup

  1. Before switching on, confirm the water supply is open, the softener/filter line is connected with no leaks, and the drain line is properly positioned.
  2. Open a steam knob, then turn the main switch to position 1. Wait for the boiler to auto-fill to its set level (probe-controlled) — this can take up to ~90 seconds.
  3. Once filled, turn the switch to position 2 — this powers the heating element.
  4. Close the steam knob once steam starts coming out, and watch the boiler pressure gauge: it should settle and hold at 0.8–1 bar.
  5. The machine is ready once boiler pressure is stable — let it sit at temperature for 15–20 minutes before pulling shots for guests.

If the boiler doesn't finish filling within the timeout, the pump stops and the keypad LEDs flash — turn the switch to 0, then back to 1, to resume filling. Before every session, visually check: power plug fully seated, water inlet open, no visible leaks, drain hose clear.

Pulling Shots

  1. Insert the portafilter into the group by twisting counter-clockwise to lock it in.
  2. Press M1 for a short/normal single, M2 for a long single, M3 for a short/normal double, or M4 for a long double.
  3. M5 starts and stops a continuous manual pour, for a free-poured shot outside the programmed volumes.

Steam & Hot Water

Steam: turn the knob counter-clockwise to open, clockwise to close. Nozzles are ball-jointed and swing or retract — use caution, risk of burns.

Hot water: press M6 to start, press again to stop. Delivery auto-stops after 4 minutes or 4 litres as a safety cutoff regardless.

Check the boiler pressure gauge shows 0.5–1 bar before drawing hot water or steam.

Programming Dose Volumes (SED)

  1. On the left-most group, hold M5 for more than 5 seconds. All M5 LEDs across groups start blinking.
  2. Press the dose button to program (M1–M4). Let it pour to the target volume, then press that same button again to save.
  3. Repeat for each of the 4 dose buttons. The hot water button (M6) can be programmed the same way.
  4. Once the left group is programmed, the other groups automatically copy those settings — any group can still be reprogrammed independently afterward.

If a dose button's LED blinks after pressing it, that signals an electronic fault or a lack of water supply — dispensing still auto-stops after 4 min / 4 litres regardless.

Pre-Infusion (SED, Single-Dose Only)

Pre-infusion wets the puck for 0.6 sec, then pauses 1.2 sec before full extraction.

To enable. with the machine off, turn the switch to 1 while holding M1 on the left group until the M5 LED stays lit, then release M1. Turn the switch to 0, then back to 2, to save.

To disable. same process, holding M2 instead of M1, then power-cycle the switch to save.

Daily Backflush (Each Group)

  1. Scrub the group head seal and dispersion screen with a group brush to clear loose grounds.
  2. Place a blind (rubber or solid) filter basket into the portafilter.
  3. Add a small, pea-sized amount of commercial espresso machine cleaning powder (e.g. Cafetto or Puly Caff) into the blind filter.
  4. Lock the portafilter tightly into the group head.
  5. Press buttons 1 and 5 together to start the automatic wash cycle. Let it run through its pre-set cycles — it will cycle water and pressure on/off several times and stop by itself.
  6. Remove the portafilter, rinse it thoroughly under clean water, and dump out any dirty residue.
  7. Rinse. lock the same blind filter — no detergent this time — back into the group head. Press buttons 1 and 5 again to run a clean-water rinse cycle.
  8. Once the cycle finishes, remove the portafilter and wipe down the group area. Repeat the full backflush and rinse sequence for every group head.

Other Daily & Closing Tasks

  1. Rinse the filter basket and portafilter with hot water after the last coffee of the session. Replace if damaged, worn or clogged.
  2. Remove the drip tray and grid frequently — clean off coffee residue and standing water to avoid odor or fermentation buildup, and run hot water through the drain to flush the tray.
  3. Clean the exterior body and steel panels with a soft sponge or cloth only. No abrasive powders, solvents or steel wool — they will scratch the steel.

Periodic Maintenance

TaskFrequency
Replace inline water filter cartridge~Every 3 months (adjust to water usage/quality)
Flush boiler (fill/drain cycles) + run water & coffee to wasteEvery 2–3 months, or after any period of disuse
Water softener regenerationPer softener manufacturer's schedule
Check power cable conditionRegularly — replace only via a Sanremo service center

A water softener/filter is not optional: unfiltered or hard water will damage internal components (pump, boiler, solenoid valves) and shortens the machine's life. Keep the inline filter clean — a clogged filter can starve the pump and cause cavitation damage.

Critical Don'ts

  • Never run the pump dry — this overheats and destroys the pump, and damage from dry-running is not covered under warranty.
  • Never clean with a water jet, and never submerge the machine.
  • Don't install or operate near heat sources or outdoors.
  • Keep the machine level for safe operation, in an ambient temperature of 5°C–35°C.
  • The service area behind the panels is for trained personnel only — always disconnect power before removing any panel.

Basic Troubleshooting

SymptomLikely CauseWhat to Check
Machine won't power on / boiler won't fillPower failure or no water supplyCheck plug/outlet, confirm the water main is open and the supply line has no leaks or kinks.
Keypad LEDs flashing after startupBoiler didn't fill within the 90-sec timeoutCycle the main switch: 0 → 1 to restart the fill.
Dose button LED blinks when pressedElectronic fault or lack of water supplyCheck the water supply; if it persists, call a qualified Sanremo service tech.
Water/steam delivery stops on its ownBuilt-in 4-minute / 4-litre safety cutoffNormal safety behavior — restart delivery as needed.
Boiler pressure not holding 0.8–1 barPressure switch needs adjustmentTechnician-only adjustment via an internal screw — don't DIY unless trained.
Noisy pump / pressure irregularPossible pump misalignment, dirty filter, or scale buildupCheck/replace the impurities filter; if persistent, call service — don't run the pump dry.

For any fault not listed here, or if a fix doesn't resolve the issue, contact a qualified Sanremo service center — do not open the machine body; always unplug it first if inspection is needed.

Daily Checklist

Opening

  • Confirm water supply open, no leaks
  • Power switch: position 1 → wait for boiler fill → position 2
  • Confirm boiler pressure settles at 0.8–1 bar
  • Let the machine sit ~15–20 min to stabilize before first shots
  • Purge steam wands briefly

Closing

  • Backflush all groups with blind filter + cleaner, then rinse cycle
  • Rinse filter baskets and portafilters
  • Remove and clean drip tray/grid
  • Wipe down exterior with soft cloth — no abrasives
  • Wipe steam wands, purge once more
  • Visual check of power cable and water lines for damage/leaks
III

Steaming Milk

Milk Texturing

Milk texturing is achieved by combining air and steam near the surface of the milk as it expands, until the desired texture is reached. Different drinks call for different textures — dry for a cappuccino, wetter for a latte — so proper technique is essential to get good, consistent results every time.

Before You Start

Drink Size. This relates to the pitcher size and how much milk you'll be using — use the right pitcher and portion your milk to the drink, to help reduce waste.

Milk Temp. The ideal range for dairy is 145°F–155°F. Standard dairy alternatives can usually tolerate a maximum of about 145°F before breaking down in texture; "Barista" style alternatives can typically withstand higher temperatures and texture well.

Milk Texture. Texturing is a race against temperature — know before you start whether the drink calls for a dry, velvety texture (like a cappuccino) or a wet, silky one (like a latte).

Setup & Target

Target Temperature (Dairy)145°F – 155°F
Dairy Alternative — Max Temp~145°F (higher for "Barista" style alternatives)
Pitcher Fill (before steaming)1/3 – 1/2 full
Starting Position — Tip DepthJust below the surface, pitcher angled left or right — never centered

Technique

  1. Choose the right size steaming pitcher for the drink.
  2. Portion the milk to the drink's size and texture; use a measuring device if needed.
  3. Purge the steam wand into the drain tray for a couple of seconds to clear any condensation.
  4. Get into the Starting Position: wand tip just below the milk's surface, pitcher angled left or right (never centered) so the milk can whirlpool.
  5. Steam with enough pressure to create a gentle vortex — too little pressure causes a high-pitched squeal or rumble.
  6. As the milk starts to whirlpool and expand, slowly draw the pitcher down along the wand, keeping the tip just submerged near the surface.
  7. Once the texture is right, submerge the wand fully and continue heating to the target temperature.
  8. Turn off the steam wand.
  9. Set the pitcher aside.
  10. Purge the wand and wipe it clean with the wand towel.
  11. Groom the milk. this step is often skipped, but it finishes the texture, not just the look. Tap the pitcher on the counter, then swirl until the milk has a glossy sheen, like melted ice cream or wet paint.
  12. Pour into the center of the drink or crema.
  13. Clean the pitcher immediately — never put a dirty pitcher back in the fridge.
Never re-steam milk that has already been steamed — for quality control and to avoid health hazards.
IV

Barista Tools

The Kit on the Bar

Tools

Tamper (58 mm, flat base)
  • Distribute the grounds evenly before tamping.
  • Tamp level and firm, straight down — consistent pressure, not forced.

An off-level tamp is one of the most common causes of channeling.

WDT Tool (Fine-gauge tines)
  • Stir through the dose in a circular motion after grinding, before tamping.
  • Break up any clumps and redistribute the grounds evenly across the basket.

Especially useful on darker roasts, which clump more from surface oils.

Digital Scale (0.1 g precision)
  • Weigh the dose before grinding.
  • Weigh the shot as it pulls, to hit the target yield.

Dose, yield and time together — not the clock alone — is what makes a shot repeatable.

Milk Pitchers (12 oz / 20 oz / 32 oz)
  • Match the pitcher to the drink — a smaller pour is easier to control in a smaller pitcher.
  • Fill no more than halfway before steaming, to leave room for the milk to expand.

Rinse immediately after each use — dried milk is the hardest to get out.

Knock Box (Rubber-lined)
  • Knock the spent puck out of the portafilter with a firm, single motion.
  • Empty and rinse it out through service, not just at close.

A full knock box slows everyone down — empty it before it's overflowing.

Puck Screen (58 mm)
  • Place on top of the dose before tamping.
  • Wipe clean between shots; it keeps the group head cleaner and reduces channeling.

Not a substitute for a good distribution and tamp — it just keeps the mess contained.

Cleaning Kit (Blind basket, group brush, detergent)
  • Backflush daily per The Espresso Machine's Daily Backflush steps.
  • Brush the group head daily; deep-clean the shower screen and gasket weekly.

A clean group head is a taste issue before it's a hygiene one — old coffee oils turn rancid fast.

Workstation Setup

Lay the station out in the order of the shot — grinder, portafilter, tamper, machine — left to right (or mirrored, for a left-handed bar), so every shot moves in one direction without doubling back.

Keep the knock box within arm's reach of the grinder, not the machine — pucks get knocked out right after grinding a new dose, not after pulling a shot.

Separate cloths by task: one dry for wiping the steam wand, one damp for the group heads and drip tray, and never the two swapped — milk residue on a group-head cloth spreads dried milk instead of removing it.
